A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, tables and complete Appendices A–D are readable and support a reliable comparison, including v2's added experimental section.

before.justification: v1 presents theoretical bounds, comparisons of published guarantees and mathematical proofs. Neither its main text nor its appendices report original empirical results.

after.justification: v2 Section 5 reports the authors' gradient-descent experiments on noisy 2-XOR data, with original test-error measurements in Tables 2–3.

M1.justification: The ReLU architecture, logistic objective, symmetric initialization, fixed output weights and gradient-descent update are retained. Evaluating a two-layer instance does not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: v1 has no empirical dataset coverage. v2 introduces training and evaluation on the explicitly constructed noisy 2-XOR binary-classification distribution, adding the paper's first experimentally studied task.

E2.justification: Neither version experimentally evaluates competing methods against the studied gradient-descent procedure. Tables 2–3 contain only that procedure; Table 1's added Lei et al. comparison concerns published theoretical guarantees.

E3.justification: v2 introduces two evaluation protocols using width 128, 500 iterations and step size 0.1: varying n over eight values from 10 to 28 at d=6, and varying d from 7 to 12 at n=64. Evaluation covers all 2^d distribution points. These experimental settings are absent from v1.

E4.justification: Tables 2–3 add controlled sample-size and input-dimension sweeps to investigate the predicted d^2/n dependence. These constitute the first empirical scaling and sensitivity analyses; v1 contains no corresponding numerical checks.

E5.justification: Neither PDF reports empirical run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. v2's new tables provide point estimates only, while the theoretical probability guarantees are retained.

E6.justification: v2 adds fourteen test-error measurements. Table 2 reports 0.4625 at n=10 and 0.2062 at n=28 with d=6; Table 3 reports 0.0125 at d=7 and 0.4190 at d=12 with n=64. v1 has no matching empirical results, so these are new observations rather than cross-version performance improvements.

T1.justification: v2 adds the noisy 2-XOR example and specializes Theorem 3 to a stated O(d^2/n) bound using the cited relation 1/gamma=O(d). The main assumptions, Theorems 1–3 and their proofs are retained. Appendix A's arbitrary-set K and cardinality N notation clarifies the already-used finite-set covering argument.

C1.justification: The abstract, three principal contributions and conclusion retain the same optimization guarantee, reduced width requirement and near-optimal sample/margin rates with polynomial depth dependence. The new experiments support these retained claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: Section 5 newly interprets the experimental errors as approximately 0.15d^2/n and as consistent with Theorem 3. The existing limitations and future directions concerning SGD, behavior far from initialization and other network architectures remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds the first experimental reproduction information: explicit data construction and normalization, network width, iteration budget, step size and exhaustive population evaluation. It also states that experiments used Google Colab and supplies a repository address for a reproduction notebook; v1 has no corresponding experimental or code-access information.

R1.justification: v2 adds Lei et al. [2024] on optimal shallow-ReLU rates to the introduction, related work, Remark 6 and Table 1. It also revises the quoted Chen et al. [2021] generalization-rate margin factor from gamma^-2 to gamma^-1. The broader positioning around deep ReLU networks remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 inserts an Experiments section and acknowledgements, renumbers the conclusion, adds short prior-work passages and clarifies Appendix A's point-set notation. Most original prose and the existing section sequence are retained; the preprint footer becomes a NeurIPS 2025 footer.

P2.justification: v2 adds two compact experimental tables and a Lei et al. row to Table 1. The existing comparison-table design and overall single-column layout are retained, with accompanying page reflow rather than a substantial visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The new numerical illustration, reproduction information and fuller prior-work discussion modestly improve the paper's inspectability and positioning while preserving its central theory. The benefit is limited: experiments use only two-layer networks and report no uncertainty, and Table 3's d=7 error of 0.0125 poorly matches the stated 0.15d^2/n approximation, about 0.115. This overstatement limits the added empirical support without outweighing the modest gains in illustration and transparency.
